newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt missing summit because of Israel -- Moussa.
newsitem.headline: Egypt missing summit because of Israel -- Moussa.

text.p: Egypt decided to skip the Middle East summit in Washington when it saw that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would be inflexible, Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in an interview published on Tuesday.
"It was clear that he does not want to move and does not want to change his attitude. All his positions were constant and total 'noes'," Moussa told the London-based newspaper al-Hayat.
"If this was the position he was going to take in the summit, then the summit...would meet with rejection, serious rejection by Israel," he added.
"Was it to be expected that (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat would move or be moved? One can't expect Arafat to be squeezed and so make concessions.

"What's needed is that Netanyahu should move. This is the essence of the summit. If that's not possible, if U.S. policy will not move him and the prestige of the U.S. president will not move him, then what would our role be?" he said.
Moussa said Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak decided early on not to attend the Washington summit. "It was his decision from the start, when he saw that Netanyahu would not move."
"We hope that our expectation is wrong but on present calculations Netanyahu will not move," he added.
